reasoning: The PKGBUILD contains only static variable definitions at the global scope with no executable code. All sources are pinned to specific versions with SHA256 checksums and point to official AWS locations (awscli.amazonaws.com and GitHub). The package() function performs standard operations (file installation, symlink creation). The .install hook only prints an informational message. No malicious code, network requests to untrusted hosts, or supply-chain risks detected.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen3-235b model (HTTP 400 API failures during full file review), not by genuine security concerns. The model's initial PKGBUILD audit was successful and found it safe. The deepseek-v4-flash model completed all reviews successfully and found the package safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory and doesn't count as a vote.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO in the full review phase, despite successfully completing the initial PKGBUILD audit
learnings: Distinguish between tool errors (API failures) and genuine security uncertainty when determining verdicts
When initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but subsequent file reviews fail, leverage the successful initial audit rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient API errors to avoid incomplete audits
